questions.answer: For a body in rotational equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point.
accepted_alternatives: The exact controlled accepted alternatives in 9702_def_principle_of_moments.
questions.tolerance: Equivalent wording must preserve rotational equilibrium and equality of both totals about the same point.

option_feedback.A: Changing angular speed is not rotational equilibrium, so the balance condition does not apply.
option_feedback.B: Correct. It includes rotational equilibrium, both directional totals and one common point.
option_feedback.C: The balance concerns moment totals, not equality of the largest individual forces.
option_feedback.D: Both totals must be calculated about the same point.

questions.answer: The clockwise couple torque is 16 x 0.40 = 6.4 N m. Rotational balance gives W x 0.50 = 50 x 0.35 + 6.4, so W = 47.8 N. A couple torque is already the force times the separation between its lines of action and is independent of the chosen point.
questions.unit_policy: Torque and moments require N m; W requires N.
questions.tolerance: Accept W from 47.8 N to 48 N with consistent working.
